findings.message: Source fetched via Archive.org fallback (original returned 200)
Instrument list misattributes two telescopes that were not used to gather the study's observations
findings.details: The body states the research team 'drew on observations from the 100-meter Effelsberg radio telescope, CSIRO's Australia Telescope Compact Array, the Very Long Baseline Array, and SKA telescopes,' citing the MPIfR press release. The MPIfR/CSIRO press releases and the full arXiv preprint (arxiv.org/pdf/2604.19435, read in full by the Chief Editor beyond the abstract page captured in the snapshot) confirm only the Effelsberg 100m telescope and ATCA were used for the new observations, plus archival data from LOFAR, ASKAP, GB6, NVSS, FIRST, VLASS, RACS, GLEAM, and Swift XRT/UVOT. The Very Long Baseline Array and SKA are explicitly described in the sources as future/upcoming instruments for follow-up work ('In the future, high-resolution instruments such as the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) will make it possible to map the structure of the jet...'; 'With sensitive facilities like the incoming SKA telescopes, we'll be able to identify similar radio transients in future sky surveys'), not telescopes that contributed to this study's dataset. Table 3 of the preprint, listing every observation used, does not include VLBA or SKA.

content_preview.title: Astronomers Catch a Nearby Black Hole in a Years-Long Radio Outburst Never Seen Before, Offering a Window Into the Early Universe
content_preview.summary: A low-mass black hole in a spiral galaxy 1.8 billion light-years away has stayed radio-bright for at least eight years, a transition astronomers say has never been observed before.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) at 563 words, within the 400-1200 range. Neutral, clear prose with no sensationalism or AI self-reference. Technical content (radio luminosity, X-ray photon index, SED turnover frequency) is presented accurately and in appropriate depth for a general-science News piece.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 sources were read from the local gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-07/astronomers-catch-a-nearby-black-hole-in-a-years-long-radio-outburst-never-seen-before-offering-a-window-into-the-early-universe/: source-0.html.gz (MPIfR press release, primary), source-1.html.gz (CSIRO/ATNF press release, a syndicated companion piece to the MPIfR release), source-2.html.gz (phys.org, fetched via Archive.org fallback per manifest — content matches MPIfR release nearly verbatim, live URL also returned 200 so no live-URL concern), source-3.html.gz (Universe Today, independent write-up with additional co-author/institution detail), source-4.html.gz (arXiv abstract landing page for 2604.19435). Because the arXiv snapshot only captures the abstract landing page (not the full paper text), and the article cites several precise numeric specifics from the paper's body (monochromatic radio luminosity 7x10^40 erg/s at 4.85 GHz; SED turnover frequency ~2.1 GHz; X-ray photon index ~2.5), I additionally fetched and read the full arXiv PDF (arxiv.org/pdf/2604.19435, all 20 pages) via WebFetch to independently verify these specifics beyond what the committed snapshot contains. All three numeric specifics, and the verbatim quote 'remarkably long-lived' (Sect. 8, Summary and Conclusions: 'the radio outburst is remarkably long-lived. It has lasted at least 8 years at roughly constant flux density'), were confirmed exact matches in the full paper. All direct quotes attributed to Komossa, Edwards, and Rose were confirmed verbatim in the MPIfR/CSIRO/Universe Today snapshots. One inaccuracy was found and is documented as a Factual Accuracy finding above and in the corrections record: the body's claim that observations were drawn from 'the Very Long Baseline Array, and SKA telescopes' in addition to Effelsberg and ATCA is incorrect — both VLBA and SKA are described in every source (press releases and the full preprint's Table 3 of observations) as future/upcoming instruments, not ones used to gather this study's data.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: With the one exception noted above (VLBA/SKA misattribution, a subordinate methodological detail in the body, not in the headline/summary/lead), every claim, figure, and quote in the article traces cleanly to a cited source. The headline, summary, and lead ('shining exceptionally brightly in radio light for more than eight years... never been observed before') are fully supported by the MPIfR press release and independently corroborated by CSIRO, phys.org, and Universe Today. No hallucinated or fabricated specifics were found elsewhere.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; appropriately hedges the unresolved physical mechanism in the 'What We Don't Know' section rather than overstating certainty.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Checked src/content/articles/2026-06 and 2026-07 for overlap; the closest recent black-hole coverage (Milky Way black hole wind, June 15; Little Red Dots/GLIMPSE-17775, June 16; Euclid ancient quasars, July 9) covers unrelated objects and findings. No duplicate or substantial overlap with existing coverage.
concerns: Body text states the research team drew on observations from the Very Long Baseline Array and SKA telescopes; per all cited sources (including the full arXiv preprint's observations table), these are future/planned instruments, not ones used to gather the reported dataset. Documented in a corrections record.

Two primary-institution sources (mpifr-bonn.mpg.de, atnf.csiro.au) are flagged by the automated allowlist check; parent domains mpg.de and csiro.au are already allowlisted but exact-hostname matching does not cover these subdomains. Both are unambiguously reputable (Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy; CSIRO's Australia Telescope National Facility) and their content was independently corroborated by phys.org and Universe Today. Adding both subdomains to config/source_allowlist.txt as a batch addition, consistent with prior review sessions.
recommendations: File a corrections record for the VLBA/SKA instrument misattribution per APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS workflow.
Add mpifr-bonn.mpg.de and atnf.csiro.au to config/source_allowlist.txt to prevent recurring allowlist warnings for these reputable primary sources.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A meticulously sourced, well-written News piece on a genuinely new astrophysics finding. Every specific was checked against source snapshots and, where the snapshot only captured an abstract landing page, against the full paper. The single instrument-attribution error is a subordinate body claim that does not affect the headline, summary, or lead, and is honestly correctable with a public corrections note. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
